description:
FILED s512 (Fable, 2026-10-07) by the static-parsing review (docs/static-parse-limits-review-s512.md, family C).  Probe in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s512/review/static: p06-autodie (perl 5.40.3 vs ./pcl on main 3ea47a41):

  use autodie; eval { open(my $fh, '<', '/nonexistent/x') }; print $@ ? "died\n" : "silent\n";       perl died   PCL silent

What autodie does in perl: at compile time its import (Fatal.pm) installs, in the CALLER's package, replacement subs for the named built-ins (`open`, `close`, `opendir`, `unlink`, `rename`, `system`, ... -- the `:default` list) that call the built-in and die with a structured autodie::exception on failure; the replacements are LEXICALLY scoped through %^H (a `no autodie` or the end of the block restores the built-in).  So it is the #2779 family (a replaced built-in with the built-in's argument count) plus the %^H scoping (not-supported.md: hints are file-global in PCL) plus a module that reads prototypes back (#2533 mentions Fatal/autodie).

What PCL does today: `use autodie` finds perl's core autodie.pm in @INC and transpiles it; its import runs; nothing is installed (why, exactly, is the first measurement: Fatal.pm builds the wrappers with string evals of generated code -- #2870's family -- and reads `prototype("CORE::open")`), and no diagnostic says so.

ROUTE (decide before building): (a) a `lib/autodie.pm` shim that registers the replacements through the builtin-override registry (`Pl::Environment::builtin_override_target`, #1870/#1992: an import LIST override is a compile-time spelling PCL already honours) with file-level scope (the %^H caveat documented) and dies perl-shaped (`Can't open '/nonexistent/x' for reading: 'No such file or directory' at FILE line N`); (b) until then, an ANNOUNCEMENT at `use autodie` that the pragma is not in effect (rule 12's effect-only boundary: never silent).  Bar: the autodie distribution's own t/ (core: lib/autodie/t/) rows for open/close/unlink/system, the everyday corpus, io/ companion.  Not scheduled: a correctness batch needs the USER's word.
subject: `use autodie` is SILENT: `use autodie; open(my $fh, '<', '/nonexistent/x')` dies in perl ('Can't open ... No such file'), PCL continues -- perl's core autodie.pm (a %^H lexical pragma that replaces the built-ins with dying wrappers at COMPILE time via Fatal.pm) loads and installs nothing; an everyday idiom with no shim and no not-supported entry
